title: Economic indicators: Key statistics for the UK economy
author: Sigma Capital
metaDescription: The UK economy grew by 0.6% in Q1 2026, with GDP at $4003 billion. Inflation was 3.0% in Q1 2026, and public sector net debt was 95.9% of GDP.

content.introduction: The UK economy grew by 0.6% in Q1 2026, with GDP at $4003 billion. Inflation was 3.0% in Q1 2026, and public sector net debt was 95.9% of GDP.
body:
GDP is estimated to have grown by 0.6% in January to March 2026 compared to the previous three-month period (October-December 2025). Eurozone GDP was flat (0.0%) in January to March 2026.

Services output was up by 1.5% in March to May 2026 compared to the previous year.

Manufacturing output increased by 1.5% over the same period.

Productivity across the whole UK economy increased by 0.9% in Q1 2026 compared with the previous quarter. Compared with the previous year, it was up by 0.4%. [...] Average wages excluding bonuses were 3.4% higher in the three months to May 2026 compared with the year before, and 0.3% higher after adjusting for inflation. CPI inflation for this period was 3.0%.

Data from the Labour Force Survey shows that 34.48 million people were in employment in March to May 2026, up 340,000 from a year before (but note that other data shows a fall in payrolled employees of 103,000 over the same period). The employment rate was 75.1%, down from 75.2% the previous year. [...] At the end of June 2026, public sector net debt was equivalent to 95.9% of GDP, compared to 94.5% a year before.

### Trade and exchange rates

The UK had a trade deficit of £18.6 billion in the three months to May 2026, compared to a deficit of £5.1 billion in the three months to February 2026.

The current account deficit was £22.1 billion in Q1 2026 (2.8% of GDP), down from £27.2 billion in Q4 2025 (3.5% of GDP).
